steps.message:
# The doors in the video misbehave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a row of doors on a test bench, each set between a small room and whatever
is on its far side. Several things about these doors go wrong in this clip: in their warning lights,
in the way a door moves, and in what ends up on each side of a shut door.

Fix every problem you find in the clip that does not match the expected behavior below.

### Expected
- A shut door keeps what is on one side from reaching the other, and its warning says what kind of
  danger it is holding back.
- The warning only shows while the door is shut.
- A door shuts smoothly, as a whole.
- Everything else should keep looking and behaving as it does now.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

Inspect the attached video before making changes. You can pull individual frames out of it with
`ffmpeg`.

/// Companion component to <see cref="DoorComponent"/> that handles firelock-specific behavior, including

/// retaining pressure..
/// </summary>

    /// Pry time modifier to be used when the firelock is currently closed due to fire or pressure.
    /// </summary>

    /// </summary>

    /// The cooldown duration before a firelock can automatically close due to a hazardous environment after it has
    /// been pried open. Measured in seconds.
    /// </summary>

    public bool Temperature;

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether the airlock is powered.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField, AutoNetworkedField]
    public bool Powered;

    #endregion

    #region Client animation

    /// <summary>
    /// The sprite state used to animate the airlock frame when the airlock opens.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField]

/// <summary>
/// Companion component to <see cref="DoorComponent"/> that handles firelock-specific behavior, including

[RegisterComponent, NetworkedComponent, AutoGenerateComponentState]
public sealed partial class FirelockComponent : Component
{
    #region Settings

    /// <summary>
    /// Pry time modifier to be used when the firelock is currently closed due to fire or pressure.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField]
    public float LockedPryTimeModifier = 1.5f;

    /// <summary>
    /// Maximum pressure difference before the firelock will refuse to open, in kPa.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField, GuidebookData]
    public float PressureThreshold = 20;

    /// <summary>
    /// Maximum temperature difference before the firelock will refuse to open, in k.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField, GuidebookData]
    public float TemperatureThreshold = 230;
    // this used to check for hot-spots, but because accessing that data is a a mess this now just checks
    // temperature. This does mean a cold room will trigger hot-air pop-ups

    /// <summary>
    /// If true, and if this door has an <see cref="AtmosAlarmableComponent"/>, then it will only auto-close if the

    /// </summary>
    [DataField]
    public bool AlarmAutoClose = true;

    /// <summary>
    /// The cooldown duration before a firelock can automatically close due to a hazardous environment after it has
    /// been pried open. Measured in seconds.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField]
    public TimeSpan EmergencyCloseCooldownDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2);

    #endregion

    #region Set by system

    /// <summary>
    /// When the firelock will be allowed to automatically close again due to a hazardous environment.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField]
    public TimeSpan? EmergencyCloseCooldown;

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether the firelock can open, or is locked due to its environment.
    /// </summary>
    public bool IsLocked => Pressure || Temperature;

    /// Whether the firelock is holding back a hazardous pressure.

    /// <summary>

    public bool Temperature;

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether the airlock is powered.
    /// </summary>
    [DataField, AutoNetworkedField]
    public bool Powered;

    #endregion

    #region Client animation

steps.message:
I found six bugs behind what the clip shows and fixed all of them. The server and client both build, and the 63 door, airtight and firelock integration tests pass. I couldn't run the game, so I haven't seen a new recording of the test bench.

**Gas getting past a shut door (column 6)**
- `Content.Server/Atmos/EntitySystems/AirtightSystem.cs`: `SetAirblocked` only refreshed the atmosphere tile when a door *opened*. When a door closed, the tile stayed open to air, so gas spread to both sides of a shut door and drew over it. It now refreshes the tile both ways.

**Warning shown on an open door, and the wrong or missing warning**
- `Content.Shared/Doors/Systems/SharedFirelockSystem.cs`: the warning visuals never updated when the door changed state, so the open firelock in column 2 kept its pressure warning. They now update on every open or close. A door that isn't shut also turns off its pressure and temperature warnings.
- `firelock.yml`: the glass firelock (column 4) uses its own set of sprite layers, which left out the pressure and temperature warning layers. That's why it showed nothing while holding back lava. I added both layers.

**Door not closing smoothly (column 6)**
- `firelock-base.rsi/meta.json`: the firelock's `closing` frames were timed 10× faster than `opening` (about 0.05s against 0.49s). The door appeared to snap shut, and its closing light flashed after the door was already closed. The timings now match `opening`.
- `Content.Client/Doors/DoorSystem.cs`: when a door that was mid-opening switched to closed, it played the *opening* animation. It now plays the closing one.
- `SharedDoorSystem.cs`: `OnPartialOpen` timed the second half of opening with the close timer (`CloseTimeTwo`) instead of `OpenTimeTwo`.

**Left as they are**
- **Column 1 (space)** shows the orange temperature warning. Space is both a vacuum and close to absolute zero, so the door is holding back both dangers. When both warnings are on, the temperature one is drawn on top.
- **Column 5 (edge firelock)** looks the same from start to finish, so I treated it as correct.
